title: Takshashila University Confers Honorary Doctorates on K. S. Chithra and S. Ramakrishnan at 2nd Convocation
summary: Takshashila University near Tindivanam awarded degrees to 312 graduates and honorary doctorates to K. S. Chithra and S. Ramakrishnan at its 2nd Convocation.
body_html:
Tindivanam, 19 November 2026: Takshashila University at Ongur, near Tindivanam, held its 2nd Convocation Ceremony on 19 November, at which honorary doctorates (Honoris Causa) were conferred on Padma Bhushan awardee and playback singer K. S. Chithra and Sahitya Akademi Award-winning Tamil writer and screenwriter S. Ramakrishnan, in recognition of their contributions to music, literature and cinema.

The ceremony was presided over by Shri M. Dhanasekaran, Chancellor of Takshashila University. Dato’ Seri Maimunah Mohd Sharif, former Executive Director of UN-Habitat and former Mayor of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, was the Chief Guest, and His Excellency U Aye Min Htwe, Ambassador of Myanmar to India, attended as the Special Guest.

The proceedings opened with the academic procession, Tamil Thai Vazhthu and the ceremonial lighting of the lamp. Dr. S. Senthil, Registrar, gave the welcome address, after which Dr. Vivek Inder Kochhar, Vice-Chancellor, presented the University's Annual Report, outlining its academic progress, research initiatives and infrastructure development.

Addressing the gathering, Shri M. Dhanasekaran said, “A university's true achievement lies not only in the degrees it awards but also in the values, knowledge and sense of responsibility it instils in its students. As we celebrate our second convocation, we are proud of our graduates and their accomplishments. Honouring distinguished personalities such as K. S. Chithra and S. Ramakrishnan also reflects our belief in recognising excellence and inspiring future generations to pursue their aspirations with dedication and purpose.”

In all, 312 graduates received their degrees across various disciplines, comprising 310 undergraduate and postgraduate students and two Ph.D. scholars. To recognise academic excellence, the University awarded 19 gold medals and four silver medals, which were presented by the Chief Guest, the Special Guest and the Chancellor.

K. S. Chithra, whose career spans nearly five decades, has contributed widely to Indian music through playback singing in several languages and through Carnatic music, and has mentored young singers on television programmes such as Vijay TV's Super Singer. S. Ramakrishnan has contributed to contemporary Tamil literature and cinema through novels, short stories, plays and screenplays that explore culture, society and human relationships.

The ceremony was attended by the University's Pro-Chancellors, Dr. D. Nila Priyadharshini and Shri D. Rajarajan, along with deans, senior officials, faculty members, graduates, parents and guests. Dr. S. Gopalakannan, Controller of Examinations, delivered the vote of thanks, and the event closed with the National Anthem.
